cards.front: What is the rate-limiting step of fatty acid synthesis, and how does acetyl-CoA reach the cytosol?
cards.back: **Acetyl-CoA carboxylase** (needs **biotin**; activated by insulin and citrate) makes **malonyl-CoA**. Acetyl-CoA leaves the mitochondria as **citrate** (**citrate shuttle**), and ATP-citrate lyase frees it in the cytosol. **Fatty acid synthase** then uses **NADPH**.
cards.back_pt: A **acetil-CoA carboxilase** (precisa de **biotina**; ativada por insulina e citrato) forma **malonil-CoA**. A acetil-CoA sai da mitocôndria como **citrato** (**lançadeira do citrato**), e a ATP-citrato liase a libera no citosol. A **ácido graxo sintase** então usa **NADPH**.

cards.front: A child becomes lethargic and hypoglycemic after fasting during an illness, with low urine ketones. Which enzyme defect fits best?
cards.back: **Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD) deficiency** (autosomal recessive). Beta-oxidation stops early, so fasting causes **hypoketotic hypoglycemia**, vomiting and lethargy, and it can cause sudden death. Plasma shows high **C8 (octanoyl) acylcarnitine**. Management: avoid fasting.
cards.back_pt: **Deficiência de acil-CoA desidrogenase de cadeia média (MCAD)** (autossômica recessiva). A betaoxidação é interrompida precocemente, então o jejum causa **hipoglicemia hipocetótica**, vômitos e letargia, e pode causar morte súbita. O plasma mostra **acilcarnitina C8 (octanoil)** elevada. Conduta: evitar jejum.

cards.front: Why can the liver make ketone bodies but not use them?
cards.back: Liver mitochondria make ketones from acetyl-CoA (via **HMG-CoA synthase**). The liver lacks **succinyl-CoA:acetoacetate CoA transferase** (thiophorase), so it cannot activate acetoacetate. Heart and skeletal muscle use ketones early in fasting; the brain uses them mainly in **prolonged starvation**.
cards.back_pt: As mitocôndrias do fígado produzem corpos cetônicos a partir de acetil-CoA (via **HMG-CoA sintase**). O fígado não tem **succinil-CoA:acetoacetato CoA transferase** (tioforase), então não consegue ativar o acetoacetato. Coração e músculo esquelético usam cetonas no início do jejum; o cérebro as usa principalmente no **jejum prolongado**.

cards.front: What does each key apolipoprotein do?
cards.back: **A-I**: activates **LCAT** (HDL). **B-48**: chylomicron assembly in the gut. **B-100**: VLDL secretion and binding to the **LDL receptor**. **C-II**: cofactor for **lipoprotein lipase**. **E**: liver uptake of chylomicron remnants and IDL.
cards.back_pt: **A-I**: ativa a **LCAT** (HDL). **B-48**: montagem dos quilomícrons no intestino. **B-100**: secreção de VLDL e ligação ao **receptor de LDL**. **C-II**: cofator da **lipase lipoproteica**. **E**: captação hepática de remanescentes de quilomícrons e de IDL.

cards.front: What do lipoprotein lipase, LCAT and CETP do?
cards.back: **Lipoprotein lipase** (on capillary endothelium) hydrolyzes triglycerides in chylomicrons and VLDL. **LCAT** esterifies free cholesterol in HDL. **CETP** moves cholesteryl esters from HDL to apoB lipoproteins in exchange for triglycerides.
cards.back_pt: A **lipase lipoproteica** (no endotélio capilar) hidrolisa os triglicerídeos dos quilomícrons e da VLDL. A **LCAT** esterifica o colesterol livre na HDL. A **CETP** transfere ésteres de colesterol da HDL para as lipoproteínas com apoB, em troca de triglicerídeos.

cards.front: Fabry disease: which enzyme, which substrate, and what are the key findings?
cards.back: **α-Galactosidase A** deficiency (**X-linked recessive**), so **ceramide trihexoside** (Gb3) builds up. Boys and young men have burning pain in the hands and feet, **angiokeratomas** and **hypohidrosis**; carrier women can also be affected. Later come **renal failure**, cardiomyopathy and stroke.
cards.back_pt: Deficiência de **α-galactosidase A** (**recessiva ligada ao X**), com acúmulo de **ceramida tri-hexosídeo** (Gb3). Meninos e homens jovens têm dor em queimação nas mãos e nos pés, **angioqueratomas** e **hipoidrose**; mulheres portadoras também podem ser afetadas. Depois surgem **insuficiência renal**, cardiomiopatia e AVC.

cards.front: How do Hurler and Hunter syndromes differ?
cards.back: Both store **heparan sulfate** and **dermatan sulfate**. **Hurler**: **α-L-iduronidase**, autosomal recessive, **corneal clouding**, coarse face, developmental delay. **Hunter**: **iduronate-2-sulfatase**, **X-linked recessive**, milder, **no corneal clouding**, hyperactivity and aggressive behavior.
cards.back_pt: Ambas acumulam **heparan sulfato** e **dermatan sulfato**. **Hurler**: **α-L-iduronidase**, autossômica recessiva, **opacificação da córnea**, fácies grosseira, atraso do desenvolvimento. **Hunter**: **iduronato-2-sulfatase**, **recessiva ligada ao X**, mais leve, **sem opacificação da córnea**, hiperatividade e comportamento agressivo.

cards.front: What are the key features of Zellweger syndrome, X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy and Refsum disease?
cards.back: **Zellweger**: no working peroxisomes; hypotonia, seizures, hepatomegaly, early death. **X-ALD** (*ABCD1*): **very-long-chain fatty acids** build up, causing adrenal insufficiency and demyelination in boys. **Refsum**: **phytanic acid** builds up; retinitis pigmentosa, neuropathy, ataxia.
cards.back_pt: **Zellweger**: sem peroxissomos funcionais; hipotonia, convulsões, hepatomegalia, morte precoce. **X-ALD** (*ABCD1*): acúmulo de **ácidos graxos de cadeia muito longa**, causando insuficiência adrenal e desmielinização em meninos. **Refsum**: acúmulo de **ácido fitânico**; retinose pigmentar, neuropatia, ataxia.

questions.stem: A 9-month-old boy is brought to the clinic because he is losing skills. At 6 months he could sit without support and reach for toys; now he cannot hold up his head. He startles strongly at ordinary sounds. Exam shows hypotonia. The liver and spleen are not enlarged. Funduscopic exam shows a cherry-red spot in the macula of both eyes. Which substance is most likely accumulating in his neurons?
questions.explanation: Developmental regression, an **exaggerated startle** to sound, a **cherry-red spot** and **no hepatosplenomegaly** point to **Tay-Sachs disease**. Deficient **hexosaminidase A** lets **GM2 ganglioside** build up in neurons. Niemann-Pick type A (sphingomyelin) also gives a cherry-red spot and neurodegeneration, but it causes marked **hepatosplenomegaly** with foam cells.
questions.explanation_pt: Regressão do desenvolvimento, **sobressalto exagerado** a sons, **mancha vermelho-cereja** e **ausência de hepatoesplenomegalia** indicam **doença de Tay-Sachs**. A deficiência de **hexosaminidase A** leva ao acúmulo de **gangliosídeo GM2** nos neurônios. A doença de Niemann-Pick tipo A (esfingomielina) também causa mancha vermelho-cereja e neurodegeneração, mas cursa com **hepatoesplenomegalia** acentuada e células espumosas.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman has 1 year of fatigue, easy bruising, and a feeling of fullness in the left upper abdomen. She also has deep pain in her right thigh. Her mental status and neurologic exam are normal. The spleen is palpable 10 cm below the costal margin, and the liver is enlarged. Hemoglobin is 9.6 g/dL, leukocyte count is 3,100/mm3, and platelet count is 72,000/mm3. X-ray of the femurs shows widening of the distal ends. A bone marrow biopsy shows large macrophages with fibrillar cytoplasm that looks like crumpled tissue paper. Deficiency of which enzyme is most likely?
questions.explanation: This is **Gaucher disease**, the most common lysosomal storage disease. Deficient **glucocerebrosidase** lets glucocerebroside fill macrophages (**Gaucher cells**, *crumpled tissue paper*), causing **hepatosplenomegaly**, **pancytopenia** and bone disease such as the **Erlenmeyer flask** deformity. Sphingomyelinase deficiency (Niemann-Pick) also causes hepatosplenomegaly, but its macrophages are lipid-laden **foam cells**.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **doença de Gaucher**, a doença de depósito lisossômico mais comum. A deficiência de **glicocerebrosidase** faz o glicocerebrosídeo encher os macrófagos (**células de Gaucher**, com aspecto de *papel de seda amassado*), causando **hepatoesplenomegalia**, **pancitopenia** e doença óssea, como a deformidade em **frasco de Erlenmeyer**. A deficiência de esfingomielinase (Niemann-Pick) também causa hepatoesplenomegalia, mas seus macrófagos são **células espumosas** cheias de lipídios.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old boy has his third episode of severe epigastric pain that goes to the back. Serum lipase is markedly elevated. He has crops of small yellow papules on the buttocks and the backs of the arms. Funduscopic exam shows creamy white retinal vessels. A fasting blood sample looks milky; after a night in the refrigerator, a creamy layer floats on top of clear plasma. Fasting triglycerides are 3,800 mg/dL. Deficiency of which protein is most likely?
questions.explanation: A creamy top layer means **chylomicrons**. **Lipoprotein lipase deficiency** (or apoC-II deficiency) stops chylomicron triglyceride breakdown, causing very high triglycerides, **acute pancreatitis**, **eruptive xanthomas** and **lipemia retinalis**. Apolipoprotein E defects (dysbetalipoproteinemia) raise chylomicron remnants and IDL, typically with palmar xanthomas in adults. Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein deficiency (abetalipoproteinemia) causes very low plasma lipids.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma camada cremosa no topo indica **quilomícrons**. A **deficiência de lipase lipoproteica** (ou de apoC-II) impede a degradação dos triglicerídeos dos quilomícrons, causando triglicerídeos muito altos, **pancreatite aguda**, **xantomas eruptivos** e **lipemia retiniana**. Os defeitos da apolipoproteína E (disbetalipoproteinemia) elevam remanescentes de quilomícrons e IDL, tipicamente com xantomas palmares em adultos. A deficiência da proteína microssomal de transferência de triglicerídeos (abetalipoproteinemia) causa lipídios plasmáticos muito baixos.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man comes for a routine exam. He has firm, painless nodules on both Achilles tendons and on the extensor tendons of his hands. There is a white ring at the edge of both corneas. His father died of a myocardial infarction at age 42. Fasting LDL cholesterol is markedly elevated, and triglycerides are normal. Which protein is most likely defective?
questions.explanation: **Tendon xanthomas**, early **corneal arcus**, isolated high LDL and premature coronary disease in a parent point to **familial hypercholesterolemia**, most often an autosomal dominant **LDL receptor** defect. The liver clears less LDL from plasma. Apolipoprotein E defects raise both cholesterol and triglycerides (remnant particles) and typically cause palmar crease and tuberoeruptive xanthomas rather than tendon xanthomas.
questions.explanation_pt: **Xantomas tendíneos**, **arco corneano** precoce, LDL isoladamente alta e doença coronariana precoce em um dos pais indicam **hipercolesterolemia familiar**, geralmente um defeito autossômico dominante do **receptor de LDL**. O fígado remove menos LDL do plasma. Os defeitos da apolipoproteína E elevam colesterol e triglicerídeos (partículas remanescentes) e tipicamente causam xantomas palmares (nas pregas) e tuberoeruptivos, e não xantomas tendíneos.

notes.title: Lipid metabolism: fatty acids, lipoproteins and storage diseases
notes.body_md:
## Fatty acids

- **Synthesis** (cytosol): **acetyl-CoA carboxylase** makes malonyl-CoA; acetyl-CoA leaves the mitochondria as **citrate**; fatty acid synthase uses **NADPH**.
- **Beta-oxidation** (mitochondria): **CPT-I** brings long-chain fatty acids in with **carnitine**. **Malonyl-CoA inhibits CPT-I**, so synthesis and oxidation do not run together.
- **Carnitine** or **MCAD** deficiency: fasting **hypoketotic hypoglycemia**.
- Essential fatty acids: **linoleic** and **α-linolenic** acid. Arachidonic acid feeds eicosanoids (drugs acting on COX and LOX: see the pharmacology blocks).

## Ketones and cholesterol

- Fasting, starvation and **DKA** (see endocrine) increase ketone production in liver mitochondria.
- **HMG-CoA reductase** is the rate-limiting step of cholesterol synthesis; statins block it (see cardiovascular pharmacology). Bile acids: see GI.

## Lipoproteins

- **Chylomicron** (apoB-48): dietary triglycerides. **VLDL** (apoB-100): liver triglycerides. **IDL** becomes **LDL**: cholesterol to tissues. **HDL** (apoA-I): reverse cholesterol transport.
- **LPL** (needs apoC-II) frees triglycerides; **LCAT** esterifies HDL cholesterol; **CETP** moves esters to apoB particles.

## Dyslipidemias

- **Familial hypercholesterolemia**: LDL receptor, autosomal dominant; tendon xanthomas, early MI.
- **LPL or apoC-II deficiency**: chylomicrons, pancreatitis, eruptive xanthomas.
- **Dysbetalipoproteinemia** (apoE2): remnants, palmar xanthomas.
- **Familial hypertriglyceridemia**: excess VLDL.
- **Abetalipoproteinemia**: see GI.

## Lysosomal storage (enzyme, substrate)

- **Tay-Sachs**: hexosaminidase A, GM2 ganglioside; cherry-red spot, no organomegaly.
- **Niemann-Pick**: sphingomyelinase, sphingomyelin; cherry-red spot, hepatosplenomegaly, foam cells.
- **Gaucher**: glucocerebrosidase, glucocerebroside; splenomegaly, bone disease.
- **Fabry** (X-linked): α-galactosidase A, ceramide trihexoside.
- **Krabbe**: galactocerebrosidase, galactocerebroside and psychosine; **globoid cells**.
- **Metachromatic leukodystrophy**: arylsulfatase A, sulfatides; demyelination.
- **Hurler** (autosomal recessive) and **Hunter** (X-linked): heparan and dermatan sulfate.
- **Pompe**: acid α-glucosidase; glycogen in lysosomes (see glycogen storage diseases).

## Peroxisomes

- **Zellweger** (no peroxisomes), **X-ALD** (very-long-chain fatty acids), **Refsum** (phytanic acid).
notes.body_pt_md:
## Ácidos graxos

- **Síntese** (citosol): a **acetil-CoA carboxilase** forma malonil-CoA; a acetil-CoA sai da mitocôndria como **citrato**; a ácido graxo sintase usa **NADPH**.
- **Betaoxidação** (mitocôndria): a **CPT-I** leva os ácidos graxos de cadeia longa para dentro com a **carnitina**. O **malonil-CoA inibe a CPT-I**, então síntese e oxidação não ocorrem juntas.
- Deficiência de **carnitina** ou de **MCAD**: **hipoglicemia hipocetótica** no jejum.
- Ácidos graxos essenciais: **linoleico** e **α-linolênico**. O ácido araquidônico origina os eicosanoides (fármacos que atuam na COX e na LOX: ver os blocos de farmacologia).

## Cetonas e colesterol

- Jejum, inanição e **CAD** (ver endócrino) aumentam a produção de cetonas nas mitocôndrias do fígado.
- A **HMG-CoA redutase** é a etapa limitante da síntese de colesterol; as estatinas a bloqueiam (ver farmacologia cardiovascular). Ácidos biliares: ver GI.

## Lipoproteínas

- **Quilomícron** (apoB-48): triglicerídeos da dieta. **VLDL** (apoB-100): triglicerídeos do fígado. A **IDL** vira **LDL**: colesterol para os tecidos. **HDL** (apoA-I): transporte reverso do colesterol.
- A **LPL** (precisa de apoC-II) libera triglicerídeos; a **LCAT** esterifica o colesterol da HDL; a **CETP** transfere ésteres para as partículas com apoB.

## Dislipidemias

- **Hipercolesterolemia familiar**: receptor de LDL, autossômica dominante; xantomas tendíneos, IAM precoce.
- **Deficiência de LPL ou de apoC-II**: quilomícrons, pancreatite, xantomas eruptivos.
- **Disbetalipoproteinemia** (apoE2): remanescentes, xantomas palmares.
- **Hipertrigliceridemia familiar**: excesso de VLDL.
- **Abetalipoproteinemia**: ver GI.

## Depósito lisossômico (enzima, substrato)

- **Tay-Sachs**: hexosaminidase A, gangliosídeo GM2; mancha vermelho-cereja, sem visceromegalia.
- **Niemann-Pick**: esfingomielinase, esfingomielina; mancha vermelho-cereja, hepatoesplenomegalia, células espumosas.
- **Gaucher**: glicocerebrosidase, glicocerebrosídeo; esplenomegalia, doença óssea.
- **Fabry** (ligada ao X): α-galactosidase A, ceramida tri-hexosídeo.
- **Krabbe**: galactocerebrosidase, galactocerebrosídeo e psicosina; **células globoides**.
- **Leucodistrofia metacromática**: arilsulfatase A, sulfatídeos; desmielinização.
- **Hurler** (autossômica recessiva) e **Hunter** (ligada ao X): heparan e dermatan sulfato.
- **Pompe**: α-glicosidase ácida; glicogênio nos lisossomos (ver glicogenoses).

## Peroxissomos

- **Zellweger** (sem peroxissomos), **X-ALD** (ácidos graxos de cadeia muito longa), **Refsum** (ácido fitânico).
